children: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand is expected to raise the official cash rate by 25 basis points to 2.75% at its policy meeting, citing a need to lower inflation and achieve a more neutral stance. The hike is likely to be accompanied by hawkish guidance. An increase in the OCR would come even as unemployment sits at its highest level in more than a decade and while global shocks threaten to impact activity and confidence. Still, RBNZ Governor Anna Breman has indicated her desire to bring inflation back to target. The policy announcement will be made at 0200 GMT. (james.glynn@wsj.com; X @JamesGlynnWSJ)
